caveats: Hand-built APPROXIMATE points only — no survey-grade post locations exist in any public source. Every feature carries location_precision='approximate' and thpo_required='yes'. Coordinates are placed on the named geographic features (point tips, bay center, city centroid), NOT on excavated or surveyed post sites; do not use for ground disturbance, navigation to a site, or any claim of exact location. Company attribution follows the sources verbatim: the Cass County Museum marker names no company per post, so Oak Point, Headquarters Bay, and Leech Lake Village/Walker are recorded as NWC/AFC (unattributed). Dates: only Otter Tail Point (c. 1785) and Pine Point (1833) carry dates from Nute 1930; the marker posts are undated. NOT mapped: Nute's second NWC post 'farther to the west as late as 1805' (no named location), the second AFC fort a mile north of Johnston's house, and the contemporaneous east-shore post on Schoolcraft's map (no named point locations). No vector canoe/portage routes drawn — no public vector layer was found; the Nute map is a 1930 schematic. Wording is source text only (Nute 1930 gazetteer entries; HMdb marker inscription); no interpretive wording added. Follow-up (not a pull): georeference the Nute 1930 map as a historic-map image overlay, alongside the GLO plats. All five points are on/near the Leech Lake Reservation; display wording is Band-reviewed (thpo_required='yes').
query: Hand-built approximate points from published sources — no API pull. Sources: Nute 1930 gazetteer (Leech Lake (1) entries 54-55; Leech Lake (2) entries 56-57), Cass County Museum 'Stimulated Exploration' marker (HMdb 235799), leechlake.org History of Leech Lake, NYBG Steere Herbarium georeference for Squaw Point (47.1693, -94.574), Bell Atlas occurrence records in Headquarters Bay. Coordinates checked against the DNR Leech Lake shoreline polygon (site/data/lakes.geojson, DOW 11020300).
